entries.name: sarc_random
entries.role: DEFAULT training corpus. Grouped-random 70/15/15, siblings kept together so the parent comment never spans two splits.
entries.use_when: Use this for the three baseline algorithms and all tuning. Report its test score as the headline number; it is the one comparable to published SARC results.
entries.notes: Optimistic relative to the two stress splits: subreddit and period are both shared across train/test by design.

entries.name: sarc_temporal
entries.role: STRESS TEST — time generalisation. train <2016, val 2016-H1, test 2016-H2.
entries.use_when: Run the tuned model from sarc_random on this without re-tuning. The gap vs sarc_random is how much of the score was period memorisation.
entries.notes: 4,790 rows removed to keep parent threads on one side. Label rate differs by design (pre-2016 ~55% sarcastic, 2016 ~48%) — that drift is the thing being measured, not a bug.

entries.name: sarc_subreddit
entries.role: STRESS TEST — community generalisation. No subreddit appears in more than one split.
entries.use_when: This is the split that actually answers 'is the subreddit topic necessary?'. Train with and without the subreddit feature here and compare; on sarc_random the comparison is confounded because the model sees the same communities twice.
entries.notes: 3,274 rows removed so no parent thread spans splits. Subreddit sarcasm rate ranges 8%-79%, so train/test label balance will not match exactly. Expect the lowest scores of the three schemes; that is the point.

entries.name: news_headlines
entries.role: Cross-domain evaluation: professionally edited prose (TheOnion vs HuffPost).
entries.use_when: Train on SARC, test here to show how much of the model is Reddit-register rather than sarcasm. Also usable as a small in-domain training set of its own for comparison.
entries.notes: RE-SPLIT BY US. The upstream train/test split was 100% contaminated (every test headline also appeared in train); these are fresh stratified 70/15/15 splits of the deduplicated rows. `article_link` was dropped — it is a perfect label leak.

entries.name: tweeteval_irony
entries.role: PRIMARY cross-platform test set. SemEval-2018 Task 3A, human-annotated.
entries.use_when: The headline transfer number. Do not train on it — train on SARC and evaluate here. Official splits are preserved so results stay comparable to published work; use `test` for the reported figure and concatenate all three only if you want a larger evaluation sample.
entries.notes: Only corpus here whose labels were checked by humans rather than inferred from an author-written tag. 436 rows still contained #irony/#sarcasm/#not — stripped by the cleaner.

entries.name: figlang_reddit
entries.use_when: SARC gives exactly one parent turn, so it can only test 'context vs no context'. Use this to sweep 0 / 1 / n turns and answer sub-question 1 as a curve.
entries.notes: `context_clean` joins turns oldest-first with ' || '; `n_context_turns` gives the count. Val carved from the official train split.

entries.name: figlang_twitter
entries.use_when: Same as figlang_reddit, on the other platform — lets you separate 'context helps' from 'context helps on Reddit'.
entries.notes: Same context encoding. Val carved from the official train split.

entries.name: twitter_sarcasm_REJECTED
entries.use_when: Never. Cite the audit in the report; do not model on it.
